Class Routes<F>

java.lang.Object
forj.http.Routes<F>
public final class Routes<F> extends Object
Routes compiled into a path trie: matching costs one step per path segment, however many routes there are, instead of trying each route in turn.
  • of(Route...) builds them; F comes from where the result goes (Routes<IO> routes = Routes.of(...), or a return). Building needs no instances: the effect's Applicative is asked for only when the routes are run (orNotFound(Applicative), apply(Request, Applicative)), where F is already known. A group of only respond routes has no F in its arguments, so when it's chained straight away (Routes.<IO>of(...).through(auth)) name it.
  • orElse(Routes) merges two groups into one trie; through(Middleware) wraps a group's handlers in middleware and keeps the trie, so wrapped groups still merge.
  • orNotFound(Applicative) makes them an app that answers the rest with 404; apply(Request, Applicative) answers only matching requests.

Matching. At each segment, a literal that leads to a match beats typed segments; among typed segments, the route given first wins (a segment can parse as more than one, as 7 does for LongVar and StringVar). A dead end backtracks. When routes share a method and path, the first one given wins. A path that matches only under other methods is answered with 405 and an Allow header. HEAD isn't answered by GET routes: declare it if you serve it.
